title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is upside down and is not motivic material. It is a stray typescript leaf from the SGA 4 étale-topology text: the comparison of the 'petit' and 'gros' étale sites (SGA 4 VII §4). Grothendieck evidently reused the back of the sheet for the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes, which appear on the neighbouring pages (polarizations, Riemann algebras, compact tori).

Setting:
- X is a scheme.
- X_ét is the small étale site (étale X-schemes).
- (Sch)/X is the big site of all X-schemes with the étale topology.
- u : Et/X → (Sch)/X is the inclusion functor.
- u_X is restriction of big sheaves to the small site, F ↦ F∘u.
- u^X (written u^* in the second formula) is the extension functor from small sheaves to big sheaves.

The page opens with the tail of a preceding formula involving the structural morphism p_{X'} : X' → X. It then remarks that to make sense of 4.1(ii) one must fix a universe U and treat the big-site sheaves as U-(Ens)-valued.

Proposition 4.1:
- (i) u^X is fully faithful, so the adjunction map G → u_X u^X(G) is an isomorphism for every étale sheaf G.
- (ii) For an abelian sheaf G on X_ét and F on (Sch)/X, the canonical maps are isomorphisms:
  - H^*(X_ét, F∘u) ≅ H^*((Sch)/X, F);
  - H^*(X_ét, G) ≅ H^*((Sch)/X, u^*G).
  These maps are edge maps of the Leray spectral sequence (V 5.5.1).
- Proof: u is a 'comorphisme' of sites (VI 7.3.6), i.e. it is continuous and cocontinuous, so restriction is exact and preserves injectives/flasques. One then applies VI 7.3.7 and 7.3.9.

Purpose: justify computing étale cohomology on either the big or the small site. This is standard and is in SGA 4.
errors: Typo in the original typescript: 'intorduire' for 'introduire', and 'sontx' (crossed out) for 'sont'.

The internal cross-references (V 5.5.1, VI 7.3.6/7.3.7/7.3.9) reflect a draft numbering of SGA 4. I am unsure whether they match the published numbering, where the corresponding cocontinuity/comorphism results sit in Exposés III–IV.

The first isomorphism as stated (H^*(X_ét, F∘u) ≅ H^*((Sch)/X, F) for an arbitrary big sheaf F) is too strong as literally written. The standard correct statement is that restriction to the small site is exact and sends injectives to acyclics, giving H^*(X_ét, F|_{X_ét}) ≅ H^*((Sch)/X, F). This holds because the small site is a localization-type subsite (X is a final object) and restriction commutes with cohomology. It is fine in context.

ideas.what: Comparison of cohomology of the small and big étale sites via the inclusion functor, which is a comorphism (continuous and cocontinuous) of sites; full faithfulness of the extension functor from small to big sheaves.
ideas.modern_name: Big vs. small étale site comparison (e.g. Stacks Project, 'Étale cohomology', comparison of big and small sites)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé VII §4 (Comparaison des grands et petits sites étales); comorphism results in SGA 4 III/IV

ideas.what: Use of a universe to make big-site sheaf categories legitimate.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a recycled typescript leaf of published SGA 4 material (étale site comparison, Prop. 4.1). It has nothing to do with the motivic notes around it and contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down (rotated 180°); the text is typescript, not manuscript.
'F u' should be read as F∘u (composition, i.e. restriction of F to the small site).
In (ii) the second formula's u^*(G) is the same functor as u^X(G) in (i).
The first line is a continuation of a formula from a previous SGA 4 typescript page, not of the motivic notes on page 83.
